rules.name: Java 7 diamond operator for generic type inference
rules.description: Java 7 allows replacing explicit type arguments in generic constructor calls with the diamond operator (<>). This simplifies code like new HashMap<String,String>() to new HashMap<>().

patterns.reason: Java 7 introduced type inference for generic instance creation (the diamond operator), allowing empty angle brackets <> to replace explicit type arguments when the compiler can infer them from context.

rules.verification_hint: Replace explicit generic type arguments with diamond operator (<>). Verify compilation succeeds on Java 7 with no type inference errors.

blast_class_evidence.reasoning: Every one of the 39 applied diffs rewrites only the right-hand-side generic-instance-creation expression ('new X<A,B>(...)' to 'new X<>(...)'), leaving the declared field or local type on the left byte-identical, so no calling file is ever forced to change and the rule is classified body-local with high confidence.

sites.what_changes: Local variable initializer inside the private static method oneShotComputeAggregatedMeasures (declared at line 130): only the constructor type arguments are erased (new HashMap<String, AverageMeasure>() -> new HashMap<>()); the declared local type Map<String, AverageMeasure> and the enclosing method signature stay byte-identical.

Still-unconverted flag site: this(new HashMap<String, AverageMeasure>(), new HashMap<String, Long>()) in the no-arg constructor; applying the rule erases the two argument-position type argument lists, while the delegated constructor SAMInfo(Map<String, AverageMeasure>, Map<String, Long>) at line 59 keeps both parameter types unchanged, so no overload resolution visible to another file is touched.

Field-declaration site (the interesting case): private List<CounterInfo> monitoredCounters = new ArrayList<CounterInfo>() -> new ArrayList<>(); only the right-hand side initializer expression loses its type argument, the field's declared type List<CounterInfo> is preserved verbatim, so every reader of the field elsewhere keeps compiling unchanged.

Second field-declaration site: private transient Map<String, Method> cachedMethods = new HashMap<String, Method>() -> new HashMap<>(); the field type Map<String, Method> is untouched, and the paired assignment at line 381 inside getMethod() is an ordinary statement in a method body.

Local variable inside the private static method buildAccessorsMap (line 212): List<Method> getters = new ArrayList<Method>() -> new ArrayList<>(); the declared local type and the method's return type Map<SlotKey, SlotAccessData> are unaffected.

Local variable inside the package-private static method getClassessOfInterface (line 106): List<Class> classList = new ArrayList<Class>() -> new ArrayList<>(); the method's declared return type List<Class> is not part of the edit, so callers of getClassessOfInterface see no change.

rules.name: Java 7 strings in switch statements
rules.description: Java 7 allows using String objects in switch statements. This enables converting if-else chains based on equals() comparisons on a String variable into cleaner switch statements.

patterns.reason: Java 7 added String support in switch statements. if-else chains comparing String equality with .equals() can be converted to switch statements for improved readability and performance.

rules.verification_hint: Convert if-else chains with equals() on String to switch statements. Verify compilation succeeds on Java 7 with no semantic changes.

blast_class_evidence.reasoning: Every flagged site is an if/else-if chain over a String tested inside a method, constructor, or anonymous-listener body that gets rewritten into an equivalent switch statement without touching any field type, return type, parameter type, or implements/extends clause, so no calling file has to change and the rule is classified body-local with high confidence.

sites.what_changes: First branch of the 9-branch if-chain (lines 323-340) inside the private static method getLevel(String level) declared at line 316; the chain collapses into 'switch (level) { case "severe": return SEVERE; ... }'. Nothing outside the catch block moves: the method stays 'private static int getLevel(String level)'. The recipe already produced such a switch at lines 341-... in this very file (it appended the switch without deleting the ifs and emitted unreachable 'break;' after 'return;', which is a separate correctness defect of the recipe, not a blast-radius one).

Head of a two-branch if/else chain (lines 520-530) over the local String 'exception' (line 516) inside 'protected void checkRemoteExceptions(Command response) throws DispatcherException, UnreachableException' (line 514); the branches become case labels on string constants. The parameter type Command, the void return type and the throws clause are all outside the edited region.

Two sequential ifs (lines 168 and 172) test '((String) r.getParamAt(1)).equals(...)' inside 'public Object serviceInvokation(String, String, String, Object[]) throws NotFoundException, ServiceException, IMTPException' (line 154). Converting them requires hoisting the cast into a local String selector and switching on it - a new local variable plus two case labels inside the body; the public method signature and its throws clause are untouched.

'else if (lastSelectedItem.equals(LABEL_TO_ADD_PROT))' inside an anonymous ActionListener body; the selector 'lastSelectedItem' is a private String field (line 177) that is only read, and LABEL_TO_ADD_PROT is 'private static final String' (line 178), i.e. already a valid compile-time case label - so the conversion adds a switch statement and changes no declaration. Note the sibling branch at line 439 uses reference comparison '!=' rather than equals(), which a switch would silently change in semantics; that is a correctness trap for the recipe, still confined to this method.

Single 'if (dsc.getName().equals("jade.core.security.Security"))' inside 'void bootAllServices(List services) throws ServiceException' (line 469) - not a chain at all, which is why the recipe recorded it SKIPPED ('Deferred - single branch, no convertible chain'). Even if converted, the edit is one statement in the method body; the raw 'List' parameter type is unaffected.

rules.name: Java 7 try-with-resources for automatic resource management
rules.description: Java 7 introduced try-with-resources, which ensures automatic closing of resources (InputStream, OutputStream, Reader, Writer, Connection, etc.) that implement AutoCloseable or Closeable.

patterns.reason: Java 7 introduced try-with-resources statement for automatic resource management. Objects implementing java.lang.AutoCloseable or java.io.Closeable can be used as resources. This is a modernization opportunity to simplify resource cleanup.

rules.verification_hint: Convert try-finally resource cleanup patterns to try-with-resources. This is an optional modernization — informational only.
